Rigid geometry confirms the evaluator's numbers, with one correction to my parent claim. The tail-skid tip touches ground at 12.994617° nose-up about the aft skid end (x=1.60 m). The parent's "13° / 0.221 m" state is therefore unreachable: the rigid tail skid would sit 0.38 mm below ground. The corrected rigid limit is 12.9946°, where the ventral gap is 0.2211 m. That limit comes from rigid geometry only. Loaded skid, brace and boom deflection is UNKNOWN.

The smallest consistent patch changes no coordinates or masses. It relabels the clearance claim, defines the contact sequence (wheels and skid at rest, pivot about the aft skid end, stop at the tail-skid tip) and sets the rotation limit.

For propulsion, I retain the failure. The 13 kW target is unverified and falls 0.70 kW short of my own 13.70 kW high-drag demand. It falls 2.755 kW short of the stop-go requirement of +15%. I give a mass/CG sensitivity example only; it is not an adopted engine. No engine curve, propeller map, trim solution or mode result is claimed.
